Her right leg is externally rotated with her right ankle resting across her left thigh just above the knee; the right shoe projects toward the open aisle. Leaning forward from her hips, she holds one lace end in each hand and draws the two ends taut above the tongue of that right shoe. The fingers, two lace ends, shoe tongue, ankle-on-thigh support and grounded left foot read together in the same view. The chair and desk leave open space for her elbows and lifted knee. She wears a pale blue cotton blouse with sleeves casually rolled to her forearms, a cream cable-knit vest, a charcoal pleated skirt falling to the knee, ivory ribbed socks and worn brown leather Oxford shoes. The raised knee organizes the skirt's natural folds, while the rolled cuffs free her wrists for the small task. An open canvas shoulder bag and a closed lecture notebook sit together on the adjacent desktop, ready for her to pick up. Rows of empty desks, a chalkboard with faint erased marks, and tall classroom windows make the academic setting visible. Photograph from a frontal three-quarter position at seated chest height, far enough back to include her complete seated figure, chair support and both shoes. Keep her face and the working hands on the raised shoe large enough to read, with a little aisle floor around the grounded foot. Soft late-afternoon window light shapes her face, the blouse creases and knit texture; the brown wood and pale blue fabric carry the quiet color rhythm. A natural 40 mm perspective and moderate depth of field connect her face, the shoe and the neighboring bag within one inhabited room.

assessments.A_bench: The lower seat and explicit Oxford/vest construction clarify craft, but the broader bench adds a horizontal mass and the extra material junctions compete with face-to-hand hierarchy. The baseline chair better defines this small departure interruption without turning the photograph into a construction demonstration.
assessments.B_high: The close downward relationship strengthens the glance, but the lifted face and near knees shrink the grounded shoe and ankle-thigh route in projection. The baseline chest-height view gives face and task more equal legibility.
assessments.C_sleeve: A sleeve-folding preparation gives the cuffs a clear purpose and a fluent self-directed gesture. It makes the lower-body arrangement incidental and removes the shoe as the common target tying outfit to support; the baseline links more of the scene through one practical act.
assessments.D_night: The dark exterior and reflected room lights create a strong study atmosphere and believable pause over notes. The pen-down/backrest arrangement is more static and makes clothing less consequential than the baseline lace task; night work also shifts the photograph toward a different episode.
assessments.E_digicam: Fluorescent compact-camera treatment gives a convincing informal archive feel. Its harder direct presentation weakens the quiet tactile cotton/knit rhythm and makes the glance read as a held pose; soft daylight better serves the task-led presence here.
assessments.F_elbows: Elbow-to-knee support is a coherent seated pause and clearly rests the upper body. Hands holding a notebook add less visible purpose or emerging consequence than finishing a shoe before departure, and make the shoe/clothing relation weaker.
assessments.G_temple: The temple target is legible without diagnosing distress and could make a quiet thinking pause. It is a more isolated face gesture and gives the surrounding clothing and bag less functional connection than the lace action.
assessments.H_crossarm: The forearm-elbow-chin chain gives a strong formal contour and a readable contact. Its stationary reflective presentation turns the classroom into backdrop and has less immediate task continuity than the baseline.
assessments.I_supine: The bench-supported back and flexed knees could make a relaxed study break. It reorganizes the entire posture and space rather than providing a restrained refinement, and the raised knees compete with face/hands while the clothing study becomes secondary.
assessments.J_retire: The standing support leg and flexed working ankle create an articulate balancing pose. It reads more as an exercise or deliberate pose than an ordinary departure task; the desktop hand support and bag grip have less natural shared purpose than the baseline shoe work.
assessments.K_sidebend: A lateral reach connects the two desks through the notebook. That extended gesture spreads the scene over two targets and weakens the compact face-hand-shoe grouping; the baseline concentrates purpose without the reach.
assessments.L_heel: The lifted heel and grounded forefoot plausibly accompany packing the bag. Their contact is farther from the acting hands, so the support reads as incidental stance while the baseline clothing object is itself the task target.
assessments.M_lowseat: The low seat permits the full bent-leg M and an ordinary lace task. Both raised knees compete with the face and crowd the skirt; the asymmetrical baseline support gives a cleaner viewing route to the same practical action.
assessments.N_polo: Polo, real pleats and sports socks make a coherent casual academic variant. The shorter sporty silhouette is a legitimate open alternative, but the blouse/knit/rolled-cuff combination gives a richer tactile rhythm and directly frees the acting wrists.
assessments.O_artpaper: Powdery marks on the open notebook give a clear art-class trace and preserve the photographic medium. It introduces a second small surface-detail target with no stronger connection to shoe tying than the existing closed notebook ready for departure.
assessments.P_lantern: An internally glowing paper lantern can warm the nearby figure and objects coherently. It introduces an additional light-object narrative with little reason for being central to this daytime departure pause; window light is more grounded in the room.
assessments.Q_bookface: The two book grips and visible eyes create an intelligible camera-facing game. It hides much of the reference face and replaces the practical task with deliberate concealment, reducing the particular face-plus-embodied-action experience.
assessments.R_gothic: Still doll-like form and a firmer editorial attitude produce a strong graphic classroom portrait. The rigidity makes the student demonstrate a presentation rather than inhabit the current task; the observational baseline has a clearer reason for the moment.
assessments.S_halfkneel: The opposite knee/foot supports and both hands at the forward shoe create a plausible alternative. It moves the clothing and contact event onto the classroom floor, expanding the lower frame and making the skirt-floor relationship an additional issue; the chair-supported baseline keeps this small departure pause more self-contained. This is preference within open staging, not a requester ban or inferred native permission.
